subject.title: sandbox: keep workspaceAccess none workspaces writable

question: Should `workspaceAccess: "none"` allow writes inside its isolated sandbox `/workspace` by default, or should it remain a read-only/no-filesystem profile?
rationale: The fix is mechanically clear, but the current behavior came from a merged security-boundary PR and is pinned in tests, while docs and tool availability now suggest `none` is isolated rather than read-only.

options.title: Approve isolated-writable none
options.body: Change Docker and sibling sandbox backends so `none` mounts the isolated sandbox workspace writable, keep `ro` read-only, update docs/tests, and force container recreation through the mount-format/config hash path.

options.title: Keep none read-only
options.body: Treat `none` as a no-write profile and update docs, tool availability, and diagnostics so write/edit/apply_patch are not offered or implied for that mode.

options.title: Defer to custom-bind design
options.body: Leave this issue open until the broader least-privilege writable-bind design in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/59718 settles, accepting that write-heavy sandbox skills remain blocked in the meantime.

recommendation.title: Approve isolated-writable none
recommendation.body: Change Docker and sibling sandbox backends so `none` mounts the isolated sandbox workspace writable, keep `ro` read-only, update docs/tests, and force container recreation through the mount-format/config hash path.

likelyOwner.reason: Best available routing candidate because he merged the PR that set the current mount semantics and is already tied to this sandbox decision surface.
